questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A destination with a high academic integrity that provides me with knowledge. Secondly the university is large with a healthy student culture which further motivated the studies. Combined with sport and leisure activities this was the perfect choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely perfect. You grow as a person and develop friendships that span countries and time.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Super easy. Erasmus university offer plenty of guidance online and via various instagram profiles that does their best to guide you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Budy program was introduced beforehand if I had any questions I knew where to direct them. Recieved mails from the adminstration that were were helpful. Also before the exchange began concerning housing and so forth.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find student housing. The hard part was fighting with a lage amount of other students to get it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: SSH offer accomodation for a fair price. Put in an effort to live in student housing so as to make friends easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty straight forward. You could look up all the offered classes and make your choices. What would have been a little more effective would be to group the 5 different master courses in diffent colours to better understand what courses were connected to each other.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Received a mail with all the relevant information from host university. Send a mail with requested subject and received all my requests.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Constant online assistance was ready. Now that Corona measures are limited, it is also possible to just show up at the administration building and ask your questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% successful. Only disadvantage was, that some of the most exiting courses were placed in block 3 and 4. I did 10 point in each. In retrospect I would do 20 point in first block and then spend more time exploring host countries in following nmonths.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask if you have questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses varied in level compared to UCPH. The general course was worth 5 point compared to a danish 15 point course. I greatly appreciated receiving teaching from experienced professors in most of my classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied greatly from teacher to teacher. Same approach with discussion and a blend of lectures and seminars

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Company law and restructuring
Private int. law
investment and trade law
int. health law
advanced trademark law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Advanced intellectual property law. Expert professor. Unique teaching style. Company law and restructuring. Amazing professor and a great amount of skilled external lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a little more expensive. When you are on exchange, you also drink a large amount of beers and want to do as many things as possible. Therefore restaurant, travel and good times drain your wallet. But it is worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: 10% more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: erasmus sport is now renovated and offer class facilities, gym and a ton of activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Multiple events hosted by university and various student organisations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get the fitness subscription from erasmus and do as much different sport as possible. It also includes padel board, bouldering and padel.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel NL. There are way too many amazing cities close by train. And bring your swapfiets bike with you. And get the museum card for 60 € so you can visit allmost every museum in NL

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do events and sports

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You deal with a lot of different cultures at the same time, especially from other int. student. Stuff like organising dinner was the most inconvenient. But in general everybody is on the same page.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Culture in the sun. Everybody just relaxed and enjoyed themselves.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Participate actively in academic work
Join as many activities as possbile.
Time moves fast so have as much fun as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure to join ESN Rotterdam immediately.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships and a deep fondness of the NL

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid in the beginning and challenge socialising. Staying in a dark room is not good for the mental health.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
